techStack: Test runner: Vitest 3.2.4 with jsdom; @testing-library/react 16, user-event 14, jest-dom 6
Context API: React.createContext with custom useFilterContext() hook that throws if used outside provider
Prop type convention: 'type Props = { ... }' (type alias, not interface); named default exports
noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters are enabled — removing a prop from a type that still references it will cause a build error
Package manager: npm with pnpm filter syntax used in test/build verification commands
No barrel/index files — all imports use explicit relative file paths
features: ProductListPage holds duplicate localSortBy state (line 31) that is disconnected from FilterContext.sortBy — SortSelect changes never reach useFilteredProducts
ProductListPage passes onCategoryClick={() => {}} (empty no-op) to ProductList (line 97) — category button clicks do nothing
SortSelect accepts two props: value (SortOption) and onChange (SortOption => void); its interface does not need to change, only what ProductListPage passes it
ProductList threads onCategoryClick from its own Props down to ProductCard — must be removed from its Props type and its ProductCard render call
ProductCard declares onCategoryClick?: (category: string) => void and calls it on button click — must be replaced with direct useFilterContext().setCategory call
FilterContext exports sortBy, setSortBy, category, setCategory, clearFilters among others — all already available to any component via useFilterContext()
useFilteredProducts reads debouncedSearch, category, inStockOnly, sortBy from FilterContext; applies filters then sort; all four are useMemo dependencies
clearFilters() resets sortBy to 'default' — once SortSelect is wired to context, clear-filters will automatically reset the sort UI too
Features that must not regress: search filtering, category filtering, inStockOnly filtering, pagination, clear filters, saved filters, product detail panel
architecture: Component tree for affected path: ProductListPage → ProductList → ProductCard
ProductListPage is the page container; it pulls from useFilterContext() and useProductContext(); it owns the layout and coordinates children
ProductList is a pure list renderer; it maps products to ProductCard; it should not own or thread filter-related callbacks
ProductCard is a leaf component; it renders one product and should own its own filter interactions via useFilterContext() directly
useFilterContext() is the correct import from '../context/FilterContext' (relative path, no barrel)
No barrel/index files exist anywhere in src/ — no index files to update when prop signatures change
After fix: ProductListPage passes sortBy/setSortBy from context to SortSelect; ProductList and ProductCard have no onCategoryClick prop; ProductCard imports and calls useFilterContext directly
edgeCases: aria-label='Filter by ${product.category}' on the category button is required — contextMigration tests locate the button via getByRole('button', { name: /filter by electronics/i }); removing or changing it breaks tests
The category button element (className='card-category category-filter-btn') must remain present for every product (requirement 8)
Calling setCategory with the currently-active category is safe — React detects no state change and does not re-render; no toggle logic needed
Sort and category filter are independent and compose: filterProducts applies category first, then sort; both come from FilterContext; wiring both correctly handles the simultaneous-filter case
clearFilters already resets sortBy to 'default' in FilterContext — once SortSelect reads from context, the sort UI resets automatically when filters are cleared (clearFilters.test.tsx covers this)
TypeScript strict mode (noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters) means localSortBy must be fully deleted (both declaration and all references) — a partial removal causes a build error
After removing onCategoryClick from ProductCard and ProductList Props types, any remaining reference in ProductListPage (the no-op prop) must also be removed — otherwise tsc errors on unknown prop
